page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.metal-48xl is a compute-optimized bare-metal server powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 architecture. The system provides 192 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, utilizing a single thread per core to eliminate simultaneous multithreading overhead. Direct hardware access without hypervisor virtualization ensures consistent processing execution across all 192 vCPUs. The server is configured with 384 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2 GB per core.

Network throughput is a defining characteristic of the c8gn.metal-48xl, offering a 600 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for high-throughput distributed data transfer. The server contains no integrated local storage drives, requiring external network-attached block storage for operating system installations and data volumes. The platform does not feature discrete GPUs, focusing hardware resources purely on CPU-bound processing, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Given its combination of dense core scaling and exceptional network capability, the server provides high resource density for scale-out compute tasks. The balanced 1:2 memory-to-core ratio prioritizes high compute utilization over memory-resident caching. The c8gn.metal-48xl is well aligned with workloads such as high-performance computing clusters, distributed network appliances, parallel batch processing, media encoding pipelines, and large-scale container orchestration.
